proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemRecord + passive_property family
proposed_widenings.justification: No magic_item kind exists in UnitRecord. The cloak is a worn item with an always-active passive property (not a spell, class feature, or mastery). A new top-level record kind and a mechanics family for passive worn/attuned effects are both required.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While you wear this cloak, it magically projects an illusion that makes you appear to be standing in a place near your actual location, causing any creature to have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.

proposed_widenings.name: on_damage_taken_window
proposed_widenings.justification: The suppression of the displacement property is triggered by the wearer taking damage. The v4 window inventory has on_hit_window (attacker side) but no window that opens when the bearer of an effect receives damage. The cloak's temporary-disable mechanic requires this trigger.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you take damage, the property ceases to function until the start of your next turn.

proposed_widenings.name: condition_gate (Speed = 0 suppression)
proposed_widenings.justification: The cloak is suppressed whenever the wearer's Speed is 0. This is a continuous runtime-state predicate, not a windowed event. The current atom vocabulary has no gate or suppress condition tied to a numeric movement-speed check.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This property is suppressed while your Speed is 0.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_advantage on incoming attacks (attachment direction: self as target)
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing modify_roll_advantage atom applies to rolls made by the bearer. The cloak's effect must apply disadvantage to rolls made by OTHER creatures targeting the bearer. The current surface schema's attachment grammar has no way to express 'attack rolls whose target is self'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: causing any creature to have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you

notes: Primary blocker is structural: magic_item is not a member of UnitRecord. Secondary blockers are (a) no passive-wear mechanics family — items don't have casting times, spell slots, or activation costs; (b) no on_damage_taken_window for the suppression interrupt; (c) no condition-gate atom for Speed=0. All four widenings would be needed to encode this unit cleanly.
